structured_output.world_model:
W5 (contrarian), after E032. Tip E027: 219 steps, 5.878 s, 0.7547 on seeds 0–2, about 0.7526 held-out.

(1) Facts read from the code that the hypotheses get wrong:
- Muon applies no weight decay at all, and it renormalizes the filters every step. So E016's wd ×0.5 changed only the SGD groups, which settles H1.5.4 by reading the code.
- Newton-Schulz already uses 3 steps.
- prepare already transfers uint8 and normalizes on the GPU, so most of I053 is already done.
- The whitening bias's lr goes to 0 at step 75 (34% of steps), but its requires_grad stays True. Every step therefore still pays for the whitening GELU backward at 31×31 and the input-grad of group 1's first conv. That waste is part of why E028 saved so much more than its MAC share.
- Group-1 BN runs after the pool, at 15×15, so BN folding (I057) saves little. The 31×31 cost sits in conv1 and the whitening GELU, not in BN.

(2) Luck: any change to the dynamics, however small, makes the per-seed endpoints diverge. A changed recipe therefore regresses to about 0.7526 on seeds 0–2, plus its own true effect and noise (SD ≈ 0.15 pp on the 3-seed mean). Only bit-identical changes keep 0.7547, and even a rebuild shifts the mean by about ±0.05 pp (E019).

(3) Time: about 23 ms per step; a frozen-stem 32 px step saves about 14 ms. Backward truncation near the stem is the remaining big lever. Epoch cost is about 0.48 pp/s at the margin.

(4) The schedule's timing is tuned (E029, E030, E032 all lost). Regularization knobs are a flat plateau.

forecasts.reason: Freeze saves about 0.85 s on 58 frozen steps; +12 steps costs about 0.28 s. +0.5 epoch adds about +0.2 pp, which roughly offsets the freeze cost and the loss of the tip's seed luck.

uint8 transfer and GPU normalization already exist in the code; only trial 0's first-call warm-up remains, about 0.03–0.05 s on the mean. Math-identical, so the per-seed results should be close to bit-identical.

The bias stops at 34% of steps, not before 25%, so the run goes ahead. Wasted whitening GELU backward and conv1 dgrad on 31×31 maps make this a real 2–4% saving. Accuracy regresses to the held-out level, and seeds 0–2 likely fall below 0.753.
35 more frozen steps save about 0.4 s. Group 1 trained 15% less costs roughly 0.1–0.3 pp. Forecast assumes the I052 successor as base.
No recipe change, so the measured numbers are a tip rerun. Pooled 20-seed mean is likely about 0.7525, below 0.753.
Group-1 BN runs at 15×15 after the pool, not 31×31. Forward-only BN savings are under 1%. Eval-mode BN shifts the dynamics and the final stats.
Diagnostic, so the measured numbers are a rerun. E028's outsized saving implies the stem is bandwidth-heavy, with non-GEMM work at 30% or more.
Muon is load-bearing for CIFAR-100 under-fitting. SGD at 219 steps and batch 2000 is likely to lose 0.5 pp or more. Dropping Newton-Schulz saves about 3%.

cruxes: How much of E028's −0.84 s came from removing the wasted whitening-bias backward (requires_grad stays True after lr reaches 0 at step 75), and how much from group-1 weight grads? If the whitening part dominates, I054 plus the freeze stack sub-additively.

Is a math-identical change (I053) actually bit-identical per seed, or does a fresh build re-select kernels and decorrelate the endpoints (E019 shifted the mean by about 0.03 pp)? This decides whether bit-identical systems wins can preserve the tip's seed luck.
Does the freeze plus 9.25 epochs (I052) reach a held-out mean of at least 0.7545? That sets whether the frozen-stem budget can be spent on epochs, or whether the population mean stays below 0.753.
